therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: NYHA Class II heart failure patients on standard heart failure therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: First occurrence of CV mortality or hospitalization due to heart failure

subgroup_findings: New onset atrial fibrillation or flutter reduced: HR 0.585 (95% CI: 0.376–0.910), p=0.0175
All-cause mortality reduced: HR 0.761 (95% CI: 0.622–0.932), p=0.0081
CV mortality reduced: HR 0.757 (95% CI: 0.609–0.941), p=0.0120
HF hospitalization reduced: HR 0.576 (95% CI: 0.473–0.702), p<0.0001
All-cause hospitalization reduced: HR 0.768 (95% CI: 0.673–0.876), p<0.0001
No significant difference in fatal/non-fatal MI: HR 1.316 (95% CI: 0.839–2.064), p=0.2321
No significant difference in fatal/non-fatal stroke: HR 0.789 (95% CI: 0.443–1.406), p=0.4213
No significant difference in ICD implantation: HR 0.994 (95% CI: 0.694–1.424), p=0.9754
No significant difference in hospitalization due to hyperkalemia: HR 1.154 (95% CI: 0.251–5.312), p=0.8539
No significant difference in new onset diabetes: HR 0.885 (95% CI: 0.559–1.400), p=0.6009
safety_signals: Hyperkalemia hospitalization rate was low and not significantly different between arms
Worsening renal function hospitalization not significantly different between arms
Serious adverse events including anaemia reported in small numbers in both arms

context.indication: NYHA Class II heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
